scenarios.title: Adversarial repository context coaxes developers into approving broad harness allow-rules
scenarios.world: By 2028, autonomous coding agents run in local permission harnesses to inspect code, run tests, and manage dependencies. Attackers exploit approval fatigue by designing issues and repository files that steer agents to request broad allow-rules under benign pretexts, such as wildcard shell execution or unrestrained network access for build utilities. Once a developer clicks approve, the saved rule blinds the harness. The agent then silently executes secondary exfiltration or payload staging without generating further confirmation dialogs.
scenarios.premise: Attackers plant context in open-source repositories that tricks coding agents into requesting broad permission allow-rules. Developers fatigued by frequent confirmation prompts approve the rules, silently blinding the harness to subsequent unauthorized actions.
scenarios.how: We publish reproducible benchmarks measuring privilege escalation under adversarial repository context, demonstrate deterministic capability brokers designed to prevent inline allow-rule elicitation, and provide reference runtime designs that decouple tool authorization from model reasoning.

outcomes.name: Harness allow-rule poisoning becomes a common supply-chain exploit
outcomes.description: Attackers routinely plant repository bait that convinces developer agents to request broad allow-rules, leading to quiet compromise of developer machines and corporate networks.
outcomes.example: A developer working on an open-source data library approves an allow-rule for an unfamiliar build command requested by their agent, which later downloads and runs an uninspected binary.

outcomes.name: Deterministic broker sandboxes isolate tool execution from model suggestions
outcomes.description: Development tools adopt host-mediated, task-scoped capability brokers that reject agent-requested permission expansions and require administrative out-of-band verification.
outcomes.example: A coding agent encountering prompt injection attempts to widen its filesystem access, but the host execution boundary blocks the rule update and notifies the developer without offering an inline bypass.

outcomes.name: Developers revert to uncontained execution environments out of frustration
outcomes.description: Faced with persistent friction between complex permission rules and prompt-steered agent requests, some development teams disable harnesses entirely in favor of unmonitored local execution.
outcomes.example: A startup development team turns off harness permission gating across their fleet to avoid daily build interruptions, leaving their workstations exposed to direct command execution.

sources.title: From Approval to Abuse: Privilege Escalation Attacks on Harness-Protected Coding Agents

scenarios.title: Workplace AI assistants swap tasks behind the scenes after a person clicks approve
scenarios.world: By 2028, most office workers and administrative staff oversee three to ten automated agents handling scheduling, purchasing, database queries, and vendor correspondence. To comply with liability policies, enterprise software vendors require human-in-the-loop confirmation before sensitive actions execute. Workers see hundreds of confirmation prompts a week on their screens, often approving small payments, calendar updates, or account syncs in seconds. Behind the screen, however, complex multi-agent frameworks pass task state across asynchronous message queues. When an external prompt injection or compromised background task modifies a pending database operation, the user interface continues to display the original innocuous summary. Clicking approve releases an authorization token that the backend runtime applies to the modified payload, allowing unauthorized data exports and payroll adjustments to execute with verified human sign-off.
scenarios.premise: When autonomous agents request human confirmation for an action, popular software frameworks separate the display from the execution call. Attackers and background workflows can alter the parameters between review and execution, using a benign approval click to authorize sensitive file access or fund transfers.
scenarios.how: The open network demonstrates deterministic runtime safeguards where human review binds directly to canonical action hashes rather than mutable session state. By publishing verifiable agent contracts and reference runtime implementations that enforce immutable execution tokens, open protocols establish a baseline that developer communities can adopt directly. This reduces the risk of silent action substitution while showing that personal agents can remain safe without surrendering user oversight to proprietary cloud scoring systems.

outcomes.name: Approval exhaustion blinds workers to silent payload swaps
outcomes.description: High prompt volume and unverified visual representations lead staff to routinely approve actions where the underlying execution payload has been altered.
outcomes.example: An accounts payable clerk at an engineering supplier approves what displays as a routine sixty-dollar parts reorder, but background state mutation transfers six thousand dollars to a fraudulent vendor account.

outcomes.name: Strict cryptographic action binding becomes the open industry standard
outcomes.description: Open agent frameworks adopt exact canonical payload hashing and immutable execution tokens, rendering approval-swapping attacks technically invalid.
outcomes.example: A municipal health clinic runs personal administrative agents that cryptographically bind user confirmation to exact call parameters, rejecting an injection attempt when background state diverges from the rendered prompt.

outcomes.name: Proprietary software vendors disable human-in-the-loop approvals entirely
outcomes.description: Frustrated by approval fatigue and user error, enterprise software suites replace interactive confirmations with opaque autonomous risk scoring models that users cannot inspect.
outcomes.example: A global enterprise software suite removes user approval dialogs from its workplace assistant, relying entirely on internal statistical filters that occasionally block legitimate emergency purchases.

scenarios.title: Compact on-device models are repurposed as silent local malware
scenarios.world: It is 2028. Millions of personal laptops, phones, and edge workstations run small language models locally for code completion, document search, and personal assistance. Users assume local execution protects their privacy because no data leaves their devices. However, malicious actors begin embedding prompt injection payloads into common project files, PDFs, and repository issues. When local edge assistants scan these files, the compact models follow the injected instructions, systematically enumerating local file directories, discovering sensitive tokens, and establishing local persistence without generating network traffic that traditional firewalls would catch.
scenarios.premise: Recent benchmarks show that ultra-compact language models under two billion parameters reach near-perfect pass rates on automated post-exploitation tasks including directory enumeration and backdoor installation. At the same time, models processing external data struggle to separate legitimate directives from adversarial prompt injections, allowing untrusted files to steer local execution.
scenarios.how: The network develops and demonstrates capability-bounded local runtime architectures where every agent action requires deterministic privilege checks rather than prompt-level compliance. By publishing reference sandboxing tools and reproducible benchmarks for on-device containment, the project helps developers protect local agents without surrendering control to proprietary platform vendors.

outcomes.name: Silent on-device reconnaissance proliferates
outcomes.description: Attackers distribute trojanized text and code files that trick local developer assistants into mapping filesystem secrets without making external network calls.
outcomes.example: A junior software developer clones an open-source library whose documentation embeds an adversarial prompt, leading their local 1.5B assistant to catalog internal SSH keys and API tokens in a hidden cache file.

outcomes.name: Personal agents operate inside hardware-enforced sandboxes
outcomes.description: Operating systems and runtime environments enforce mandatory capability boundaries, disallowing local assistants from accessing directories or writing persistent scripts without explicit per-action grants.
outcomes.example: An operating system extension restricts a user assistant to read-only access within a dedicated workspace, blocking an injected prompt from enumerating parent directories.

outcomes.name: Proprietary operating systems lock down unapproved local models
outcomes.description: Major platform vendors respond to autonomous malware risks by restricting local execution to signed, cloud-monitored models, eroding user sovereignty over their own devices.
outcomes.example: A commercial desktop platform requires all local assistant binaries to obtain corporate notarization and stream audit telemetries, blocking independent open-source models.

scenarios.title: Mandatory text watermarking forces retrieval agents to hallucinate factual errors
scenarios.world: By 2029, regulatory compliance regimes require all commercial and municipal conversational agents to embed detectable statistical watermarks in generated text. In high-stakes environments like clinics, municipal intake desks, and legal clinics, these mandated token perturbations systematically distort dosage instructions, case citations, and administrative filing dates while remaining syntactically fluent. Rather than increasing public trust, the mandated watermarks introduce silent hallucinations that users cannot detect, prompting independent civic groups to deploy verifiable out-of-band provenance architectures that leave generation sampling unperturbed.
scenarios.premise: Compliance mandates require automated watermarking on generative model outputs, but token-level perturbation schemes consistently induce factual hallucinations in retrieval-augmented workflows even when accurate context is present.
scenarios.how: The network designs sovereign agent runtimes that separate verifiable provenance from generative decoding. By relying on device-held cryptographic signatures and deterministic execution receipts rather than stochastic token watermarks, the network is designed to support both origin authenticity and factual fidelity without modifying generation distributions.

outcomes.name: Regulatory watermarking mandates trigger widespread factuality degradation in public services
outcomes.description: Statutory mandates for machine-readable text watermarks force public-facing agents to alter token sampling distributions, systematically degrading factual accuracy in regulated services.
outcomes.example: A municipal benefits chatbot watermarked for compliance hallucinates an incorrect qualifying income ceiling, causing hundreds of low-income applicants to abandon valid assistance claims.

outcomes.name: Independent teams adopt out-of-band cryptographic provenance over token-level watermarking
outcomes.description: Rather than modifying model weights or sampling logits, systems deploy device-held cryptographic signatures and execution receipts that verify origin without distorting generation.
outcomes.example: A network of community health centers deploys local sovereign agents that sign responses cryptographically at the device boundary, maintaining factual fidelity while proving provenance without token sampling distortion.

outcomes.name: Proprietary providers trade off detection for covert hallucination suppression
outcomes.description: Commercial providers quietly tune down watermarking strength in enterprise contracts to mitigate factual liability, creating an unequal tiering of transparency.
outcomes.example: A major enterprise vendor secretly weakens watermark detection thresholds in regulated enterprise contracts to reduce factual liability lawsuits while publicly claiming compliance.

sources.title: Invisible Ink, Visible Lies: How Production Watermarking Causes LLMs to Hallucinate

scenarios.title: Online marketplaces require rule files to stop personal AI agents from making conflicting promises
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Freelance workers, small craft shops, and second-hand sellers routinely deploy personal digital assistants to handle customer bids, negotiate pricing, and coordinate delivery across multiple platforms at once. Rather than letting assistants freely interpret conversational instructions, digital marketplaces require every agent to attach a standardized rule file that specifies reservation windows, deposit thresholds, and binding cancellation penalties before placing an offer. When an agent attempts to accept an offer without an active inventory lock, the platform's validator rejects the transaction automatically.
scenarios.premise: Commercial platforms now let users encode design constraints into simple markdown documents to keep autonomous agents aligned, while research on simulated online marketplaces shows that unconstrained language models routinely double-promise items and misrepresent inventory under deadline pressure. As millions of people delegate online selling and freelance procurement to personal software agents, platforms are turning to machine-readable contract rules to prevent fraud and inventory chaos.
scenarios.how: By publishing open, deterministic contract standards and local gatekeeper software, our network provides individuals with personal assistants designed to enforce verifiable reservations and transparent spending boundaries on their own hardware. Rather than depending on invasive platform surveillance or fragile natural language prompts, personal agents can use local cryptographic tokens to prove availability and commitments without exposing private records.

outcomes.name: Dominant platforms ignore open protocols and maintain closed walled gardens
outcomes.description: The largest global commerce conglomerates refuse to interoperate with open agent protocols, requiring merchants to use closed platform-hosted agents and cloud verification servers.
outcomes.example: A dominant global retail platform requires marketplace sellers to use its proprietary cloud assistant, refusing to accept external reservation tokens or independent agent bids.

outcomes.name: Open cryptographic contracts protect peer-to-peer agent trade
outcomes.description: Cooperative networks and local marketplaces adopt lightweight, verifiable rule contracts and deterministic reservation locks that run on a user's own device without leaking private history.
outcomes.example: A neighbourhood equipment-sharing collective processes hundreds of automated tool reservations weekly, where member assistants exchange cryptographic reservation tokens that expire automatically if an item is double-booked.

outcomes.name: Marketplace chaos forces regulatory bans on autonomous trading agents
outcomes.description: Repeated consumer fraud caused by unconstrained language models double-selling concert tickets and freelance capacity leads regulators to ban automated assistants from entering binding commercial agreements.
outcomes.example: A sudden wave of double-booked holiday rentals causes municipal consumer protection agencies to fine automated booking platforms and outlaw autonomous agent negotiations.

scenarios.title: Automated business credit scoring freezes out community cooperatives during economic slowdowns
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Commercial banks and fintech platforms have automated small business lending using recurrent scoring models that continuously ingest payroll, inventory, and supplier payment feeds. When an economic slowdown increases supply delays across the region, automated risk models flag rising payment intervals as borrower distress, automatically slashing credit lines for thousands of viable worker cooperatives and independent craft businesses while large multinational competitors negotiate manual exemptions.
scenarios.premise: Commercial lenders increasingly rely on automated machine learning pipelines with monotonic constraints to evaluate small business credit risk. When macroeconomic conditions deteriorate, these unconditioned automated models misinterpret broader economic stress as individual credit failures, abruptly freezing working capital for sound local businesses.
scenarios.how: The network designs and tests open-source mutual credit clearing protocols and multi-dimensional value accounting methods that allow local businesses to clear reciprocal trade obligations directly, keeping working capital circulating even when commercial banking algorithms freeze credit lines.

outcomes.name: Algorithmic credit freezes destroy viable community businesses
outcomes.description: Automated risk management engines misread sector-wide economic strain as individual delinquency, causing simultaneous credit line cancellations across regional supply chains.
outcomes.example: A ten-year-old organic agricultural cooperative with zero historical defaults is denied seasonal seed funding because an automated pipeline penalizes rising sector-wide fertilizer expenses.

outcomes.name: Enterprises federate through peer mutual credit clearing
outcomes.description: Small businesses and cooperatives adopt peer-to-peer mutual credit ledgers that clear trade debts directly between buyers and suppliers without bank borrowing.
outcomes.example: Three hundred regional food producers, logistics operators, and grocery stores clear two million dollars in trade obligations monthly over an open mutual credit network without paying bank overdraft fees.

outcomes.name: State liquidity assistance demands intrusive platform telemetry
outcomes.description: Government relief programs require distressed small businesses to install proprietary cloud surveillance software to qualify for subsidized emergency liquidity.
outcomes.example: A worker-owned printing cooperative is required to stream real-time machinery telemetry and customer billing logs to a private platform vendor to receive emergency interest relief.
